findings.claim: The suspended_nonpayment next step says paying the one holding invoice restarts runs. billing_standing (20261029150000_billing.sql:248-260) picks only the oldest failing invoice (ORDER BY first_failed_at, id LIMIT 1). If a second open or uncollectible invoice also failed more than 30 days ago, paying the named invoice moves the hold to that one, and organization_run_refusal keeps refusing. RESTARTS (line 208, used at line 241) and the combined hold 'new runs stay stopped until it is paid as well' (lines 249-256) are then false. The tests only ever build one failing invoice, so they pass vacuously here.
findings.scenario: A group's monthly invoice fails by card on 2026-08-01, and the 2026-09-01 invoice fails on the same dead card. On 2026-10-05 both are more than 30 days old. The page says 'Pay SIM-0001 below. A card payment restarts runs at once'. The administrator pays SIM-0001 by card, billing_standing now holds on SIM-0002 (failed 2026-09-01, more than 30 days ago), and uploads and pricing runs are still refused with 'suspended for nonpayment'. The page now names SIM-0002 and makes the same promise again.
findings.fix: In organizationBilling (apps/worker/src/billing/account.ts:122-130), add to the organization query `(SELECT count(*) FROM invoice i WHERE i.organization_id = o.id AND i.status IN ('open','uncollectible') AND i.first_failed_at <= now() - interval '30 days')::int AS holding_count` (the same predicate the view uses) and expose it as `holdingCount` on OrganizationBilling/BillingView. In accountStanding, when holdingCount > 1, word the step as 'Pay SIM-0001 and the other N invoices unpaid for 30 days below.', and say runs restart only once all of them are paid (card at once, ACH once settled). Use the same rule for the 'until it is paid as well' clause. Add a db test with two invoices failed 31 and 45 days ago: pay the holding one, then assert that the refusal persists and the standing names the second.

findings.claim: A closed organization is told it can be reopened, but no product path reopens one. setOrganizationStatus accepts only 'suspended' | 'active' and refuses a closed organization outright ('a closed organization is neither suspended nor reinstated', apps/web/src/lib/routes/console.ts:103-105). No ADR or runbook describes reopening. organization_run_refusal's own sentence for closed is 'no new run starts', with no lift. Yet the closed next step is 'Open a support ticket to reopen it.' (line 266), planRefusal says 'open a support ticket to reopen it' (line 269), and the past-due hold says 'new runs stay stopped even once the organization is reopened' (lines 248 and 256). The closed plus nonpayment hold, 'new runs stay stopped until it is paid as well' (line 255), implies that paying restarts runs, and for a closed organization nothing does.
findings.scenario: An organization closed with an invoice unpaid for 31 days reads: 'The organization is closed: its data stays readable, and no new run starts. An invoice is also unpaid since 2026-09-01; new runs stay stopped until it is paid as well.' It pays, and nothing restarts. Its ticket asking to reopen hits a console that refuses to change a closed status.
findings.fix: For kind 'closed', drop every reopen promise. Use the next step ticket(' if you have a question about the closure.') and planRefusal 'A closed organization takes no new plan.'. For held, when closed, use ` An invoice is also unpaid since ${day}; it is still owed.` with no clause about runs, and for closed drop `lifted` entirely. Update the BIL-05 rows in docs/product/test-matrix.md, matrix.ts and fixtures/synthetic/BIL-05/expected.json ('offers the ticket to reopen it'), along with account-standing.test.tsx and the closed db test. If reopening is meant to exist, it is a Lane A console and migration change, so record it as a follow-up and do not promise it in customer copy now.

findings.claim: The past-due words 'until it is paid' (line 230) and 'unless it is paid by <date>' (line 256) treat an ACH payment as paid when it starts. billing_standing keeps first_failed_at and the open status until the bank settles, so an ACH payment started a day before the stop date still lets runs stop on that date. The suspended_nonpayment step got the ACH caveat (SS-03), but these two did not. 'paid by <date>' is also a calendar date, while the stop is the exact instant first_failed_at + 30 days (for example 15:00 UTC).
findings.scenario: Past due since 2026-10-10 15:00 UTC. The page says runs stop 2026-11-09. The administrator pays by bank on 2026-11-08, settlement lands 2026-11-11, and runs are refused 2026-11-09 to 11 even though the page implied paying in time was enough.
findings.fix: Append the same caveat to the group past-due notice and the past-due hold, for example '…until it is paid; a bank (ACH) payment counts once the bank settles it, usually within a few days.' Optionally print the stop as a UTC timestamp (utc()) instead of a date.

findings.claim: subscribe reads organization.status in its own tp_billing transaction, before currentSubscription, ensureCustomer and the claim INSERT. This is a check-then-act: a status change between the read and the claim is not seen. It is theoretical today because nothing sets 'closed', but the claim is the place that already serializes subscription starts.
findings.scenario: Once a close path exists, an organization closed between the status read and the subscription_claim insert still gets a Stripe subscription.
findings.fix: Fold the check into the claim statement: `INSERT INTO subscription_claim (organization_id, plan) SELECT $1, $2 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM organization WHERE id = $1 AND status <> 'closed') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`. Keep the early read for the specific error, and when the insert returns no row, re-read the status to pick the message.

The record's status wins over billing's standing, firms are never told runs stopped, the holding invoice is organization-scoped and payable outside the newest 24, and the closed-plan refusal and the seeded persona are sound. ux.summary:
The PR does what it claims: a suspended or closed organization no longer reads "In good standing", the standing comes from one place (standingKind and accountStanding), and the good state's screens are pixel-identical before and after. Nothing is blocking. Five should-fix defects remain:
- UX-1: the combined-hold sentence for a past-due invoice says runs "stay stopped even once PaidWhole lifts the suspension". Billing's view is live and only holds runs from the stop date, so that is false.
- UX-2: a closed organization's plan card still says "The plan amounts shown are placeholders" with no amounts shown (visible in the shots).
- UX-3: the closed organization's Invoices empty state still says to choose a plan the page refuses (visible in the shots).
- UX-4: "Closed" uses the danger tone on both screens; ADR 0056 makes a system state a neutral badge.
- UX-5: the "Pay <invoice>" anchor lands under the sticky 56px header with no scroll margin.

Four nits cover naming and wording consistency: "Suspended (PaidWhole)" in the console, the firm's billing-hold words in the console, "lifts it" against the practice home's "reinstates it", and the plan-refusal wording with the repeated closed title. The copy lint passes. Not seen in shots: the console billing page and the support page, which I judged from code.
